principles: Generic core code consumes a host-neutral owner-session result and does not learn new provider-specific env names.
Local owner-session identity is coordination metadata only and never upgrades evidence into Authority or reviewer proof.
Behavior-preserving migration comes before cleanup: existing owner-lease semantics must stay green while source labels and adapters move behind the facade.
Every persisted generated-token path must be runtime-artifact registered and material-safe.
drivers: The user needs reliable multi-host parallel development across Codex, Claude Code, Antigravity/agy, and future hosts.
The previous ppid fallback can misidentify one host session as multiple owners when each command gets a new shell parent.
The implementation touches lifecycle/owner gates, so review and tests must catch regressions mechanically.

options.name: A: Host-neutral resolver facade with adapter boundary and guardrails
pros: Meets the B-a781 target contract directly
Keeps future host onboarding out of generic owner-lease logic
Allows focused smoke and grep guardrails to prevent regression
cons: Touches several core files and requires careful compatibility for old sessionSource values
Generated-token persistence must be designed narrowly to avoid runtime artifact pollution

options.name: B: Extend current core resolver with Codex and agy env branches
pros: Would likely fix one or two current host cases quickly
cons: Creates the exact per-host core exception pattern the user rejected
Every future host would require another core branch and another regression risk
Does not clean lifecycle ad hoc env reads

options.name: C: Require users to manually export LATTICE_SESSION_ID only
pros: Leaves existing core behavior mostly unchanged
cons: Does not give host-neutral runtime support for Codex/Claude/agy users
Still leaves confusing ppid degradation as a common path
Fails the execution plan acceptance criteria for adapters and generated-token fallback

chosen: A: Host-neutral resolver facade with adapter boundary and guardrails
rationale: Option A is the only option that satisfies the user requirement to avoid Claude-only fixes and future per-host core branches while preserving current owner-lease behavior through tests.

preMortem.scenario: A host-native env name remains in generic owner-lease or lifecycle code after migration.
preMortem.trigger: Implementation moves behavior but misses an ad hoc read in context, transition, gate, or cli-engine code.
preMortem.consequence: Future host onboarding repeats the same core-branch problem and reviewer cannot prove the contract mechanically.
preMortem.mitigation: Add a guardrail task/script in the story-owner smoke suite that fails if host-native session env names appear outside adapter files/tests/docs.

preMortem.scenario: Generated-token fallback dirties git status or material hash.
preMortem.trigger: Token file is persisted under an unregistered path or a tracked metadata subtree.
preMortem.consequence: DONE or validation sees unrelated dirty material, and local coordination artifacts pollute evidence.
preMortem.mitigation: Register the token storage path in runtime-artifact-registry, ensure ignore/material classification, and cover it in the smoke test.

preMortem.scenario: The migration accidentally treats local session ids as proof of identity.
preMortem.trigger: Diagnostics or docs phrase generated/local session ids as verified actor identity or Authority evidence.
preMortem.consequence: Users may overclaim production/Authority completion from forgeable local env variables.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep source labels local/non-cryptographic in code comments/docs and add review evidence explicitly checking the local boundary.

preMortem.scenario: Existing Claude Code stable-session behavior regresses during cleanup.
preMortem.trigger: Moving CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID handling into the adapter changes trim/priority/cache behavior.
preMortem.consequence: Claude users again see false foreign-owner conflicts across Bash invocations.
preMortem.mitigation: Preserve compatibility through adapter tests: canonical env wins, blank canonical env falls through, Claude native signal remains stable across ppid changes.
